cards.back: Store each weight as the nearest mark on a coarser ruler, so it takes fewer bits: a smaller, faster model at a rounding cost you measure.
Each output adds up thousands of weights so small errors partly cancel, and most weights sit close to zero where a good ruler covers them finely.
A single large weight stretches a shared scale so small weights round to zero. Real 4-bit methods use a scale per group of 64 to 128 weights.
scale = max|w| / 127 (or 7 for 4-bit), q = round(w / scale), and at run time w′ = q × scale.

cards.front: Why a "4-bit" model uses more than 4 bits
cards.back: Each group stores a 16-bit scale; with groups of 128 that adds about 0.13 bits, so 4-bit models use about 4.1 to 4.5 bits per weight.
Each token reads every weight from memory and reading is the slow part, so halving the bytes nearly doubles single-user speed and frees room for KV cache.
An 8-bit float with 4 exponent and 3 mantissa bits. Its marks are dense near zero, which suits weights; used for weights, activations and KV cache on GPUs that support it.
4-bit weights with 16-bit activations: weight-only quantization, the lowest-risk option because the maths still runs in 16-bit.
GPTQ quantizes weights one at a time and adjusts the rest to cancel the error. AWQ finds the weights that matter most from activations and protects them with per-channel scaling.
Every method except QAT: runs on a finished model in minutes to hours with at most a few hundred calibration examples.
8-bit is close to lossless for most tasks, 4-bit with GPTQ or AWQ loses a little (more on small models), and below 4 bits quality drops quickly.

quiz.q: In 8-bit symmetric quantization, the group's largest weight is 0.98. What is the scale?
quiz.why: The scale is max|w| divided by the largest 8-bit integer, 127, giving 0.00772.

quiz.q: Many users with long contexts are filling the GPU. What do you quantize first?
quiz.why: KV cache quantization saves memory per token of context, so more users or longer contexts fit.

quiz.q: Which tasks tend to break first after quantization?
choices: Maths, long contexts, code and strict formats
quiz.why: Multi-step reasoning, long contexts, code, non-English text and strict output formats are the fragile cases.

quiz.q: Which method moves outliers from activations into weights so both fit in 8 bits?
quiz.why: SmoothQuant enables W8A8 by shifting activation outliers into the weights.

quiz.q: You must run a large model on one GPU or a laptop. What do you choose?
quiz.why: 4-bit weights cut memory to about a quarter of BF16.

quiz.q: Quality must not move at all. What's the right call?
choices: Stay at 16-bit and add GPUs or use a smaller model
quiz.why: Every quantization has some quality cost, so stay at 16-bit if nothing may change.

quiz.q: Why do weights-and-activations formats like W8A8 need careful scaling?
choices: Scales cannot be stored per group
quiz.why: Activation outliers stretch the scale, so W8A8 and FP8 need care that weight-only does not.
